title: The scope boundary is fragile prose, not a structured field
findings_note: reproduced closing S47; a section edit silently dropped it

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
The scope boundary — the `**Not in this slice:**` paragraph — is not a first-class part
of a slice. `promote` and `import` append the marker string to whatever section is *last*,
and `Slice.boundary()` finds it by scanning every section's prose for a paragraph that
starts with the marker. Three problems follow:

- **A section edit destroys it, silently.** Filing S47, `import` appended the boundary to
  its Git section; the next `slicer edit S47 --section Git` replaced that body and dropped
  the boundary, and `check` then warned that the scope was unbounded. Nothing re-adds it.
- Its position is arbitrary — "the last section", which differs slice to slice.
- `verify` detects it by scanning prose, so the check is only as reliable as the marker
  surviving in some body.

It should be set explicitly when a slice is created and stored as its own thing, so a
section edit cannot touch it — the boundary passed as an argument, not smuggled into prose.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/model.py` — a `boundary` field on `Slice`, in to_dict/from_dict
- `src/slicer/ops.py` — `promote`, `_slice_from_spec` set it explicitly; `edit_section` no longer owns it
- `src/slicer/render.py` — emit it in a fixed place
- `src/slicer/migrator.py` / `legacy.py` — parse the inline marker into the field, emit it back
- `src/slicer/verify.py` — check the field, not a prose scan

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. Editing the section that used to hold the boundary does not lose it.
2. A promoted slice's boundary survives a round of section edits.
3. `migrate` reads an inline `**Not in this slice:**` into the field and renders it back so
   the legacy tree still round-trips.
4. `verify` reports a genuinely missing boundary and passes when it is present.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Give `Slice` a `boundary` field, defaulting empty. `promote` and `_slice_from_spec` set it
to `cfg.boundary` explicitly rather than appending the marker to a section. `render` emits
it in a fixed position. `edit_section` no longer has any way to remove it. On `migrate`,
parse the inline marker out of the legacy prose into the field and render it back inline
where the format expects it, so the byte-identity round-trip holds. `verify.offline`
checks `sl.boundary` rather than scanning bodies.

The real work is the legacy round-trip: the migrate format carries the boundary inline in
a section, so the field and the inline text have to reconcile without changing the emitted
bytes.

**Not in this slice:** making the boundary configurable beyond the single `cfg.boundary`
marker; one marker is the shape the tool has.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
`slicer edit <id> --section <the one that held the boundary>` then `slicer check` stays
clean — the boundary is no longer editable prose.
